title: Rabbi Yaakov bar Abaye
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in the Yerushalmi: Berakhot ch. 2, end of halakha 3 (פ״ב סה״ג); Moed Katan ch. 3, halakha 1; Sanhedrin ch. 10, halakha 2, where he speaks in the name of Rabbi Acha; and in Megillah ch. 1, halakha 9 and in Ruth Rabbah at the end of ch. 8, the reading is 'bar Abbaiah'; and in Moed Katan ch. 3, halakha 1 and Sukkah ch. 1, halakha 6 he speaks in the name of Rav Sheshet.

And the conjecture of the Introduction to the Yerushalmi is that he is the son of Abaye, the colleague of Rava, who is mentioned in Yoma 27a, that Abaye was reviewing teachings with his son, and that he went up from Babylonia to the Land of Israel in his youth, and therefore he is not mentioned in the Bavli, end of quote. But it is very difficult to say this, because in the days of Abaye the decrees in the Land of Israel were so numerous that almost the majority of the sages of the Land of Israel went down to Babylonia with Ravin, as is explained in his entry.

And in Bamidbar Rabbah ch. 2, [par.] 26, Rabbi Yaakov bar Ivo is cited in the name of Rabbi Acha, and it should read 'bar Abaye', as in Tanchuma Acharei [par.] 19; and it is very close to say that he is Rabbi Yaakov bar Abaye of Bardelia who is mentioned in Sheviit ch. 2, halakha 4.

notes.text: Mevo HaYerushalmi suggests that this sage was Abaye’s son; Hyman expressly argues against that chronological identification.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 1:6 reads Yaakov bar Abaya in a chain with Rav Sheshet and Chiyya Rabbah. It does not establish that he was the Bavli Abaye’s son. The Mevo HaYerushalmi proposal and Hyman’s opposing chronological argument remain distinct.
